thread:
ingrid: Heads up — us-west1 GPU attach latency just spiked. Lots of pods Pending with `attach` errors, attach times went from ~10s to 90-120s.
sam: saw this on canary too. K8s attach logs show `device busy` and a bunch of `fsync` waits. Any recent scrub/cleanup jobs? :warning:
alex: digging into node iostats — iops around 220k-260k on several scratch NVMe, qdepth appears saturated.
maya: janitor started a deep-scrub sweep at 03:12 across the same shard set. That can blow up fsync churn if co-located with GPU attach windows.
raj: short-term mitigation: throttle janitor concurrency or push batch jobs off the hotstripe nodes. Long-term we should consider io-aware scheduling for attaches.
ingrid: copying the relevant tail from dmesg / attach logs:
```
[03:18:02] nvme0: internal io timeout, aborting command
[03:18:05] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
k8s: attach controller: device busy, retrying attach for vol-abc123
```
alex: also seeing SMART reassigns bumping on 3 devices (EOL-ish wear pattern). Not full failures but increased latency under heavy parallel ops.
maya: can we patch janitor to drop concurrency from 8 -> 1 as a quick canary? That should immediately reduce fsync pressure.
sam: agreed. Also can we change attach preference to prefer nodes labeled `io_health=good`? That would steer away from hotstripe nodes until scrub finishes.
ingrid: will push a canary patch now to reduce janitor concurrency. kubectl patch command I'm applying:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/janitor SCRUB_CONCURRENCY=1 --record
```
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-7893; assigned to @oncall-marc for follow-up. :rotating_light:
oncall-marc: I'm on it. If the canary reduces attach latency we can do a controlled rollback of the scrub or continue with throttling.
raj: one more note — cost tradeoff: moving these GPU requests to Dedicated capacity avoids local NVMe contention but increases committed spend. We should weigh temporary dedicated burst vs throttling janitor.
alex: for nodes with repeated SMART reassigns, recommend setting `drain=true` and reprovision from spare pool. I'll paste a drain snippet:
```
./node-admin drain --node gnode-42 --reason "nvme-reassigns"
```
ingrid: canary applied, will monitor attach latency and attach success rate. reporting back in 15m. :crossed_fingers:
sam: thanks — if latency drops, let's rollout concurrency change cluster-wide for the next 24h window and schedule a follow-up wear analysis.
ingrid: ack, updating incident and putting a hold on any heavy checkpointing jobs for the next 6h.
